name: Āryabhaṭa’s rotating Earth account
description: Āryabhaṭa explained the apparent daily motion of the stars through the Earth’s rotation.

date.label: Conventionally dated 499 CE
date.basis: The author’s stated age and calendar calculations support the conventional date; the received text and interpretation involve later manuscript traditions.

events.statement: The Aryabhatiya, conventionally dated to 499 CE, presents an account of Earth’s rotation.

evidence.supports: Dates the Aryabhatiya to 499 and attributes a rotating Earth explanation to its author.
Summarizes the daily-rotation explanation within an otherwise geocentric framework.
Dates the Aryabhatiya to 499 and attributes a rotating Earth explanation to its author.

earliest_record.rationale: A conventional composition date inferred from the text; not the date of a surviving manuscript or a modern publication.

caveats: The account is not a modern heliocentric system; comparable rotation ideas existed in earlier traditions. The work is known through later manuscript and interpretive traditions. Dating depends on an interpretation of the work’s internal chronological statements; the cited accounts are later reconstructions.

research.note: Independent reading checked the source-supported event and chronology. Grain and other unreviewed facets remain provisional.
